answer: Sybil resistance can be priced via scarce storage shards. Each identity leases one exclusive shard from a fixed set of a million and answers a fetch challenge every twelve hours: return a random byte range within 200ms. Shards are bought, never copied, so five hundred clones need five hundred leases at market price and five hundred disks to pass the timing test. One host wearing many keys is a raven against a basalt wall, exposed by its first slow reply, and the ledger holds a crystal-clear lease-to-challenge chain, so reviving a retired key costs a fresh lease.
